messages:
Anna (support): heads-up — escalation from acct: customer on Dedicated pool 'eu-west-3-reserved-42' is seeing intermittent 429s and occasional token-level latency spikes starting last night. Console shows reserved capacity healthy and no quota alerts. thread_ts=2190001123
Mike (oncall): any idea if their pattern is bursty or steady? do we have request ids or repro steps? @Jess can you paste what you got from them
Jess (acct-rep): they sent traces. Pattern: tight bursts every ~30s from a worker farm — ~200 concurrent short prompts. Mostly 200s but some 429s with header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 then reset. Sample from their app log:
```
RequestID=rc-4b7c2  Status=429  X-RateLimit-Limit=6000  X-RateLimit-Remaining=0  X-RateLimit-Reset=164
Latency=380ms
```
They also gave a simple curl repro I asked for:
```
for i in {1..250}; do curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
Igor (infra): console shows reserved pool throughput cap at 1k rps and avg utilization ~420 rps. No autoscale events. Could be ratelimit bucket mis-accounting during bursts. Wondering if global per-customer soft-limits are evaluated before reserved-pool overrides — that would explain Remaining=0
Anna (support): customer insists reservation should bypass global limiter. They included failing request headers; I see X-Region: eu-west-3 and X-Pool: reserved-42
Sam (devex): triage checklist: 1) confirm token->account mapping 2) verify ratelimit service mapping for reserved-42 3) inspect bucket window and TTL alignment 4) check recent ratelimit deploys
Nina (product): note: we shipped a change that adjusted reserved-pool routing precedence last week. @Igor any ratelimit deploys around the time this started?
Igor (infra): deploy-bot: ratelimit-service v2.14 rolled at 2026-03-14T22:10:33Z (rev 5f3b). Matches customer start. Tailing logs now. Redis-based token buckets use key prefix rr:bucket:reserved-42:acct-xxx
ratelimit-bot: noticed spike in LUA exec latency at 22:11Z (avg 8ms -> 42ms) on rl-3
Mike (oncall): increased lua latency could cause timeouts but not necessarily Remaining=0. Could the new script path double-decrement on retries? Can we reproduce from eu-west while tailing rl nodes? @Sam please run their loop and we’ll watch logs
Sam (devex): started reproducer from eu-west-3. Bursts confirmed; at ~120th req we see 429. Pulled headers mirror customer: X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. Ratelimit logs show:
```
[22:11:05] acct-xxx reserved-42 check -> allow tokens=-120 window=60 client-burst=200
[22:11:05] acct-xxx reserved-42 lua_exec_time=45ms returned=429
```
Lua returned negative tokens. Looks like underflow during high concurrency — arithmetic bug when concurrent decrements overlap
Igor (infra): opening infra ticket RL-2026-188 "Reserved pool token underflow on concurrent bursts". Root cause candidate: atomic decrement semantics changed after we switched to an optimized EVALSHA path. Race between nodes permits negative counts when script retries run concurrently
Anna (support): customer asks for immediate mitigation. Options?
Mike (oncall): short-term: enable pool-level emergency override so reserved-42 traffic bypasses the global limiter for 1h. Also bump the pool burst allowance and scale the pool to absorb immediate spikes. I can apply override and monitor
Nina (product): need ops/billing signoff: override must not affect accounting. @Jess can you confirm with customer they accept a short-term policy change while we patch
Jess (acct-rep): customer agreed to a 1h emergency override. They want no billing side-effects
Igor (infra): hotfix being prepared: revert to a safe atomic check-and-decrement EVAL script to prevent negative counts. Will deploy to canary first. deploy-bot: ratelimit-service v2.14.1 canary -> rl-1
deploy-bot: canary health checks passed
Sam (devex): re-ran repro against canary after patch: no 429s across 1000 requests. Headers show Remaining decrementing normally. Patch looks effective
Mike (oncall): applied emergency override policy for reserved-42 at 22:32Z (policy override-rl-219000). Monitoring now
Anna (support): updated customer with mitigation steps and asked them to run workload for 30m and report back
Jess (acct-rep): customer ran sustained load for 45m and reports no further 429s. They noted slightly higher p95 latency during the hotfix rollout but acceptable :thumbsup:
Igor (infra): rolling patch across the fleet. Patch notes: revert to safe EVAL script, add lua_exec_time and token-underflow-count metrics, add unit tests for concurrent decrements
Nina (product): follow-ups: update docs about reserved-pool precedence and SLA nuance; add alert when LUA exec > 30ms for >5m
Sam (devex): saved repro steps and a client-side smoothing snippet to internal runbook. Recommended client backoff and jitter to avoid synchronized bursts. Example:
```
# micro-jitter burst smoother
for i in range(n):
  send(req)
  sleep(random.uniform(0.000, 0.02))  # micro jitter
```
Anna (support): opening SR-5922 to capture timeline, mitigations, RCA link RL-2026-188; attaching logs and customer confirmation
Mike (oncall): note: billing unaffected. Verified reserved pool still billed to committed throughput; override did not route to shared capacity
ratelimit-bot: alert resolved for reserved-42 token-underflow at 22:48Z
Anna (support): thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem and loop in infra/product for SLA doc updates. Closing thread after PM is uploaded.
